name: Curaçao
instrument: Ministerial admission-policy document (beleidsstuk / beleidsregel of the Minister of Justice) modernising the toelatingsbeleid, announced as taking effect 1 April 2026 and expressly replacing the 2019 admission policy. The 2019 predecessor is the published beleidsstuk 'IMPLEMENTATIE BELEIDSWIJZIGINGEN PER 1 JANUARI 2019' (https://gobiernu.cw/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Implementatie_Beleidswijziging_per_1_januari_2019_2.pdf). The 2026 replacement text itself is not published on any official Curaçao channel found; no Landsverordening amendment, Landsbesluit or Publicatieblad/Landscourant notice carrying a 2026-04-01 effective date was located. Statutory basis is Landsverordening Toelating en Uitzetting (LTU), P.B. 2010 no. 5, art. 6(2), which fixes no maximum term for a vergunning tot tijdelijk verblijf.
quote_original: Un di e kambionan mas importante ta ku, dependiente di e propósito di estadia, aplikantenan lo por pidi un pèrmit di estadia temporal pa un periodo máksimo di tres aña.
quote_translation: One of the most important changes is that, depending on the purpose of stay, applicants will be able to request a temporary residence permit for a maximum period of three years.
transition_rules: None published. The press release states only that the new policy replaces the 2019 admission policy; it gives no grandfathering, no treatment of permits issued before 1 April 2026, and no renewal rule. By contrast the 2019 instrument it replaces did contain an explicit transition clause ('Indien men in het verleden een vergunning voor de duur van twee of drie jaren heeft ontvangen, zal bij een tijdige verlenging wederom eenzelfde duur voor de vergunning gehanteerd worden'), so the absence here is a genuine gap, not an omission on our side. Fee treatment under the 2019 policy was leges and retributies payable per year requested (aantal jaar x leges en retributies); whether that survives is unstated.
notes:
VERDICT REASONING. The monitor claim is substantially correct but its framing and its cited URLs are both wrong. (1) Of the two discovery URLs given, https://www.gobiernu.cw/ is the government homepage (HTTP 200, redirects to https://gobiernu.cw/) and https://gobiernu.cw/wet-en-regelgeving-immigratiedienst-curacao/ is a fabricated path — it returns HTTP 404 with the WordPress not-found body. Do not cite it. (2) The real official source is the Government of Curaçao press release of 19 March 2026 (WP post id 561463, post type 'nieuw', published 2026-03-19T11:47:08), located by querying the gobiernu.cw WordPress REST API rather than by search. Both quotes below were verified to appear character-for-character in the raw HTML served at source_url.

WHAT IT IS. This is a horizontal change to the default validity period of the ordinary vergunning tot tijdelijk verblijf, not a new residence product. Since 1 January 2019 the default has been one (1) year: the 2019 beleidsstuk, section 3 'Geldigheidsduur', reads 'Een vergunning tot tijdelijk verblijf is in principe geldig voor één (1) jaar.' The 2026 policy raises the ceiling to three years, conditioned on purpose of stay ('dependiente di e propósito di estadia'). The press release itself confirms the replacement relationship: 'E kambio di maneho aki ta sustituí e maneho di atmishon for di 2019' ('This policy change replaces the admission policy from 2019') — also verified verbatim at source_url. Note the historical irony: gobiernu.cw post 33945 of 2018-12-14 announced the move in the opposite direction, from 2- and 3-year permits down to 1-year permits effective 1 January 2019. The 2026 change is a reversion.

WHY THERE IS NO PRIMARY INSTRUMENT TO FIND. Permit duration on Curaçao is not fixed by statute. LTU art. 6(2) states only 'Een vergunning tot tijdelijk verblijf wordt, vrij van zegel en kosten, voor een bepaalde termijn afgegeven' — a determinate term, with no maximum. Art. 7(1) vests the grant in the Minister of Justice. Duration is therefore set entirely by ministerial policy, which is why the 2019 change was effected by a three-page beleidsstuk on TO letterhead and not by a Landsverordening or Landsbesluit. The 2026 change needs no legislative instrument, and none should be expected to exist. The gap is publication, not legality.

LANGUAGE. quote_original is Papiamentu, not Dutch. The Government of Curaçao issued this release in Papiamentu only. No Dutch or English version exists: the gobiernu.cw REST search returns no Dutch-language counterpart ('modernisering' matches only an unrelated Nieuwe Haven post), and https://gobiernu.cw/nl/nieuw/<slug> 302s back to the Papiamentu post rather than serving a translation. Dutch is the legal language but is not the language this policy was announced in.

SEARCH RECORD — what was tried and what was ruled out. gobiernu.cw WordPress REST API enumerated in full: post types 'laws' (x-wp-total: 1, a 2025 fuel-price regulation, irrelevant), 'landscourant' (x-wp-total: 44, archive stops at 2019 with one stray 2023 edition — the live Landscourant is not published here), 'document' (x-wp-total: 98, newest 2025-03-27, nothing on immigration), and the full media library searched for toelating, beleid, atmishon, landsbesluit, verblijf, permit, maneho, implementatie, wijziging, geldigheidsduur, modernisa, instructie, landscourant, 'LC Ed', publicatieblad. No 2026 immigration policy document exists in the media library. The Servisio di Atmishon 'Lei i maneho' page (https://gobiernu.cw/ministerionan/hustisia/sektor-di-mantenshon-di-lei-i-orden-publiko-i-seguridat/servisio-di-atmishon/lei-i-maneho/) is the canonical index of admission law and policy; it was fetched live and still links only the twelve 2019-era PDFs, with no 2026 addition — it has not been updated for the change it now misdescribes. Council of Ministers decision lists (post type 'konseho_niews', 40 most recent, covering 2025-09-05 to 2026-08-07) were fetched and grepped for toelatingsbeleid / maneho di atmishon / pèrmit di estadia / verblijfsvergunning / LTU / vreemdeling; the 11 March 2026 list matched only on an unrelated civil-service 'instroomplanning' item. The Toelatingsorganisatie's own site immigrationcur.org (WordPress, HTTP 200) was enumerated: all 29 pages, its media library, and REST searches for beleid, toelatingsbeleid, 'drie jaar', 2026, wetgeving, landsverordening. It carries no 2026 policy document and its product pages still state no revised duration. Its 2026 news output is entirely about the separate Rib'e Lugá regularisation project. Hosts probed: toelatingsorganisatie.cw and landscourant.cw do not resolve (NXDOMAIN); overheid.cw times out; parlamento.cw serves HTTP 200 but exposes no legislation index and 403s its wp-json. No law-firm, relocation-agency or news source was used for any factual assertion in this row.

STANDING CAVEAT. Because the operative text is unpublished, the three-year figure is the ceiling the Minister announced, not a term any applicant is guaranteed. 'Dependiente di e propósito di estadia' is doing real work: the 2019 policy tied duration for doel arbeid to the length of the tewerkstellingsvergunning and for dependants to the principal's term, and nothing in the release suggests those linkages were severed. Treat permit_max_duration_months as a maximum, not a default. Re-check the 'Lei i maneho' page for a new PDF before hardening this to confirmed_primary.

name: Curaçao
instrument: Ministeriële Beschikking 'Kapitaalkrachtige Investeerder 2014' of the Minister of Justice, 6 September 2014 (the Servisio di Atmishon 'Lei i maneho' index dates the same instrument 26 September 2014 and links a scanned copy at https://gobiernu.cw/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/MB_Kapitaalkrachtige_investeerders_NED.pdf).
quote_original: Bij een zakelijke investering vanaf XCG 500.000,00 wordt de verblijfsvergunning voor een periode van 3 jaren afgegeven.
quote_translation: For a business investment from XCG 500,000.00, the residence permit is issued for a period of 3 years.
transition_rules: Not applicable — this is the pre-existing tiered investor rule, unchanged by the 1 April 2026 policy. Tiers run 3 years from XCG 500,000; 5 years from XCG 750,000; indefinite (onbepaalde tijd) from XCG 1,500,000.
notes:
DISAMBIGUATION ROW — recorded because it is the most likely thing for a downstream reader to confuse with the 2026 claim, and confusing them would produce a wrong route edit.

Curaçao already issued three-year residence permits before April 2026, but only to capital-strength investors, and under a completely different instrument. The Toelatingsorganisatie product page states the origin verbatim: 'heeft op 6 september 2014 een vergunning voor tijdelijk verblijf of tot verblijf voor investeerders geïntroduceerd; genaamd Kapitaalkrachtige Investeerder 2014.' Duration is a function of investment size, not of the general admission policy: 'De geldigheid van de vergunning is afhankelijk van de waarde van de investering.' All three quotes in this row were verified character-for-character in the raw HTML at source_url.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ATLAS. The 36-month term on curacao-wealthy-investor-residence derives from this 2014 Ministeriële Beschikking and is therefore NOT evidence for, and NOT affected by, the 2026 change. The two are independent. A reader who treats the 2026 announcement as the source of the investor route's three-year term would be attributing a 2014 rule to a 2026 instrument.

SOURCE-TIER NOTE. Verdict is confirmed_secondary rather than confirmed_primary because the Ministeriële Beschikking PDF hosted on gobiernu.cw is a scanned image with no text layer — nine pages yielding 8 extractable characters — so nothing in it can be quoted under the character-for-character rule. source_url is therefore the administering agency's own official product page, which is authority for how the agency applies the instrument but is not the instrument. Anyone wanting confirmed_primary will need OCR of the scan or a Publicatieblad text.

MINOR CONFLICT WORTH FLAGGING. The instrument's date is inconsistent across two official Curaçao sources: immigrationcur.org says 6 September 2014, while the gobiernu.cw 'Lei i maneho' index describes the wealthy-investor policy as the 'Ministriële Beschikking van de 26ste september 2014'. Both are government pages. Not resolved here; the scan would settle it.
